title: Same Tree
spaceBreakdown:
- recursion depth: up to h nodes → O(h)  
- not counted: input trees, return value
approach: Two trees are the same exactly when their roots have equal values **and** their left sub‑trees are the same **and** their right sub‑trees are the same. A simple depth‑first recursion checks these three conditions at every node. Because each node is visited once, the method is correct and optimal.
hints:
If two trees are identical, what relationship must hold between the values at their roots and the structures beneath them?  
Each tree contains at most 100 nodes.

Use a depth‑first recursive traversal (the call stack acts as the data structure).  
For p = [1,2,3] and q = [1,2,3], compare the root (1), then recurse left (2) and right (3).

if both nodes are null → true  
if one is null → false  
if values differ → false  
return recurse(left children) AND recurse(right children)

**Both null** - both trees are empty  
`Input: p = [], q = []` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: checking only p->val == q->val without null test → dereference null → runtime error  

**One null** - one tree empty, other not  
`Input: p = [1], q = []` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: returning true when values match at root and ignoring missing child → returns true  

**Different value** - same shape but root values differ  
`Input: p = [1], q = [2]` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: using || instead of && when combining left/right results → returns true  

**Skewed left** - trees are linked‑list shaped on left side, identical  
`Input: p = [1,2,null,3], q = [1,2,null,3]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: iterative BFS with fixed queue size assuming balanced tree → may miss nodes → returns false

followUps.q: What if the trees can contain up to 10⁵ nodes?
followUps.a: The recursive version may overflow the call stack, so an explicit stack (or queue) should be used iteratively. Time stays O(n); worst‑case space becomes O(n) for the explicit container.

followUps.q: How would you change the solution to test whether two trees are mirrors of each other?
followUps.a: Compare the left subtree of one tree with the right subtree of the other and vice‑versa, recursing with those swapped children. The algorithm remains O(n) time and O(h) space.

followUps.q: Suppose node values are 64‑bit integers and you cannot rely on the provided int field.
followUps.a: Redefine the node value type to long long (or cast to long long when comparing). The traversal logic does not change, so time is O(n) and space O(h).
